Read one CSV or TSV file into a measurement record

Source: R/record-import.R
read_measure_record_delim.Rd

read_measure_record_delim() reads a single local CSV or TSV long table with strict UTF-8 and fixed column names, then delegates record construction to measure_record_from_long(). It reads the source bytes once, enforces max_bytes while reading, and records the caller-declared source ID, the input basename, and a SHA-256 digest of those exact bytes. The digest helps detect accidental changes; it does not authenticate the source or record the complete mapping and transformation history.

Usage

read_measure_record_delim(
  file,
  columns,
  source_id,
  delim = c(",", "\t"),
  allow_extra_columns = FALSE,
  max_bytes = 100 * 1024^2
)

Arguments

file

A local regular CSV or TSV file path.

columns

A named character vector mapping canonical fields to exact input header names. See measure_record_from_long() for the required and optional canonical names.

source_id

A caller-declared, nonblank character source identifier.

delim

A comma or tab field delimiter. No delimiter inference is performed.

allow_extra_columns

Set to TRUE to ignore columns not named in columns.

max_bytes

A positive whole-number byte limit for the single source file.

Value

A measure_record with one source row containing the input basename and SHA-256 digest.

Details

All fields are initially read as character. Identifiers such as 0007, 1e3, NA, and formula-like strings remain literal text. Numeric fields use a strict, locale-independent decimal grammar: locations must be finite, and signal values may be finite or missing. Blank optional metadata cells become unknown (NA_character_); literal NA remains text. Mappings, units, and identities are never inferred. Curves may have independent finite, monotone grids and are not sorted or interpolated.

Unmapped columns are rejected unless allow_extra_columns = TRUE, which explicitly opts into ignoring them. This reader covers one-dimensional curves in CSV/TSV text; it does not parse nD data, DAD/MS vendor structures, or vendor-specific formats.

Examples

csv_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
writeLines(
  c(
    "sample_id,injection_id,channel_id,curve_id,location,value",
    "sample-01,injection-01,uv,curve-01,250,0.02",
    "sample-01,injection-01,uv,curve-01,251,0.04"
  ),
  csv_file,
  useBytes = TRUE
)
csv_columns <- c(
  sample_id = "sample_id",
  injection_id = "injection_id",
  channel_id = "channel_id",
  curve_id = "curve_id",
  location = "location",
  value = "value"
)
imported <- read_measure_record_delim(csv_file, csv_columns, "source-01")
imported
#> <measure_record>
#>   Samples: 1
#>   Injections: 1
#>   Channels: 1
#>   Curves: 1
#>   Sources: 1
unlink(csv_file)
